sources.title: US Patent 392,046 (US392046A), John J. Loud, granted 30 October 1888
sources.supports: Loud's documented design (a reservoir pen with a rotating marking point for rough surfaces) and the grant date.

sources.title: German Patent and Trademark Office (DPMA): Ballpoint pen
sources.supports: Loud's patent is distinct from László Bíró's later development of a practical writing instrument and suitable ink, with his chemist brother György and others.

sources.title: Science Museum Group: Biro ballpoint pen, object 1949-174/2
sources.locator: Object record, date and makers; Rights section
sources.supports: A particular surviving Biro pen dated 1945–1948; the record names László József Bíró and his brother Georg. Image rights are asset-specific.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: Techniques of Decoration on Arms and Armor (2003)
sources.supports: Pattern welding (joining and working different iron or steel components) is distinct from crucible or watered-steel production.

sources.title: Verhoeven, Pendray and Dauksch, 'The key role of impurities in ancient Damascus steel blades', JOM 50(9), 1998, pp. 58–64
sources.supports: The study uses both 'pattern-welded Damascus' and 'wootz Damascus', so 'Damascus' alone is not one material recipe.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: Ten Wootz Steel Ingots with Bag, accession 2023.133a–k
sources.supports: Specific object metadata: Indian, probably eighteenth century. The qualifier 'probably' stays visible.
